artists.biography: Haken (/ˈheɪkən/) are an English progressive metal band formed in 2007 by multi-instrumentalist Richard Henshall, guitarist Matthew Marshall, and vocalist Ross Jennings. While Henshall, Marshall, and Jennings first had the idea of forming Haken in 2004, they opted to pursue their instruments and songwriting first. Upon recruiting other members three years later, they eventually released the demo Enter the 5th Dimension in 2008, signing with Sensory Records and releasing their first album Aquarius in 2010. As of 2020, they have released six studio albums, an EP, and two live albums.

perplexity.description:
Virus is the sixth studio album by British progressive metal band Haken, released in 2020 through Inside Out Music. Musically, the album blends progressive metal, progressive rock, and djent, showcasing the band’s signature technical proficiency, dynamic songwriting, and genre-bending experimentation. The album features a mix of aggressive riffs, intricate rhythms, lush harmonies, and playful sonic textures, with standout tracks like “Prosthetic,” “Carousel,” and “Messiah Complex” highlighting both the band’s heavier and more melodic sides. The album’s sound draws comparisons to acts like Fear Factory and Devin Townsend, while maintaining Haken’s distinct identity.

Virus serves as the second half of a conceptual rock opera, continuing the narrative begun on their 2018 album Vector. It addresses recurring themes from their discography, notably revisiting the enigmatic “Cockroach King” motif introduced on The Mountain (2013). Critics praised the album for its ambitious scope, tight performances, and ability to balance complexity with accessibility, with many placing it among Haken’s strongest works. While some reviewers noted it didn’t surpass their earlier classics, Virus was widely regarded as a high point in their catalog and appeared on several year-end “Best Of” lists in 2020.
